claims.statement: URE publishes forms and information for energy-efficiency certificate applications, including planned and completed projects.
URE's public materials include a power-of-attorney template, supporting the possibility of authorised representation in the process but not proving assignability of proceeds.

contrary_evidence: The official sources establish an application process, not commercial demand, approval speed, certificate value or the proposed revenue-share contract.

economics.acquisition_route: Unvalidated: begin with the founder's family renewable-energy company, then offer regional installers a no-upfront-cost clause and eligibility API inside quoting.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario, not a forecast: prove 20 filings in year 1, reach 1.5 million PLN annual fee revenue in year 3, 3 million PLN owner equity plus retained cash by year 5, and 5 million PLN founder net worth in years 7-9.
economics.founder_time: Unvalidated operating estimate: 2-4 hours per day until audit coordination is delegated.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unvalidated: 55%-75% gross margin after external energy-audit, filing and certificate-sale costs.
economics.payback: Unvalidated: initial capital payback in 12-24 months, highly sensitive to URE processing and project volume.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated commercial figures, including capital_required_pln: a success fee of 20%-35% of net certificate proceeds.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Unvalidated: repeat follows each partner installer's recurring retrofit pipeline; there is no validated renewal or project-frequency evidence.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Every submission links project attributes, audit assumptions, regulator outcome and realised value, improving selection and partner economics
fingerprint.customer: Polish SME building owners and renewable, HVAC and industrial-efficiency installers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: A contractual module embedded in installer quotes and sales workflows
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: End-to-end certificate origination on contingency, with expert audits procured rather than built in-house
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The project beneficiary pays an agreed share only after certificate proceeds are realised
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An eligible energy-saving project is quoted but has not yet begun

founder_fit: Directly leverages the family renewable-energy channel.
Uses quantitative screening and AI-assisted document workflows.
Can begin part-time without public-facing content.
risks: A project may be ineligible because contracting or work began too early.
Regulatory delays and certificate-price volatility can break payback.
A mistaken savings estimate could create liability.

structure.control_point: Exclusive pre-project mandates and, where counsel confirms legality, contractual assignment or collection rights over certificate proceeds from an installer network
structure.critical_dependency: Polish counsel must confirm the agency and rights structure; qualifying work must meet URE rules and be documented by competent auditors

thesis: Embed eligibility screening and an exclusive pre-project mandate into Polish energy installers' quote flow, then coordinate the audit, URE application and monetisation of energy-efficiency certificates for a contingent share. The moat is not a dashboard: it is a contracted stream of origination rights plus a growing project-to-approval dataset that improves screening and audit procurement.
title: Installer-Embedded White-Certificate Rights Rail
uncertainties: Minimum viable project size and approval rate by intervention type
Whether certificate or proceeds rights can be assigned in the preferred structure
